precedence: current cumulative render profiles and workflow

requirements.statement: The consolidated requirements baseline is the highest-level expression of user intent; structures define allowed syntax, profiles define rendering, the registry defines data, and the workflow defines execution.
When an original prompt conflicts with a later explicit user decision, the later decision prevails and the superseded rule remains documented.
Normative versions must be explicit; no validated debate package is silently migrated to a newer norm.
The active system is French-English only; Spanish or another language requires a new explicit version.
All structural choices must be persisted in files; conversation memory is never a source of truth.
Use two ChatGPT projects: Wikidéb'IA for active production and Archives de Wikidéb'IA for completed debates.
Move completed Work conversations to the archive project; generic conversation archiving is not a substitute.
A Work cannot contain another Work; all Work conversations are autonomous and of the same level.
Separate graph research, debate writing, argument writing, validation, English adaptation, interlanguage and publication into specialized Work.
Lock canonical titles in both languages after graph validation and before French page generation; English page content remains deferred until after complete French validation.
Work 03 and Work 07 batches of the same language are sequential unless an explicit future concurrency protocol is introduced.
Prefer high reasoning for ordinary production, very high reasoning for complex/final graph and validation tasks, and maximum only exceptionally when available.
The method may use a local directory but must not depend on one to function in the two-project organization.
Use only parameters and nested templates allowed by the official French and English structures.
Preserve canonical parameter order, spelling, accents, capitalization and hyphenation.
Omit every optional parameter and nested parameter that has no relevant content; mandatory parameters may never be empty.
requirements.note: Supersedes original debate-prompt instruction to retain empty parameters.

requirements.statement: Allowed-but-not-generated warning parameters remain in the structural schema but are absent from automatic output.
A newly created French Debate uses avancement=Débat construit; an existing Debate preserves the exact previous presence and value of avancement.
requirements.note: Creation and modification are distinct; no forced progress value on existing pages.

requirements.statement: A genuinely new English Debate generated from scratch uses progress=Constructed debate. In FR→EN translation, progress maps the exact French avancement value and an absent source field remains absent; an existing English target page is not an editorial translation source.
requirements.note: Translation metadata mapping overrides creation defaults for FR→EN editorial production.

requirements.statement: Exact AI warnings are added only to pages genuinely created from scratch. A generated English translation maps French title/debate/argument warning values exactly and does not add an AI warning when the French source lacks it.
requirements.note: A translation file being new does not make the translated page a new AI-created logical page for warning defaults.

requirements.statement: Do not invent nom-consacré/established-name or initialisation/initialization automatically. For every new Argument page, research whether a conventional name is attested in the literature and emit nom-consacré/established-name only when the dedicated discovery review concludes known_name; preserve legacy nom/name exactly only on attested pre-existing pages, and allow additions to preexisting pages only through an explicit owner-approved assignment review.
Do not generate citations/quotes in Argument pages.
requirements.note: Replaced from norm 1.2.27 by RND-003 and RND-004; citations may be rendered only from sealed editorial locks.

requirements.statement: Preserve an attested historical débat-détaillé/detailed-debate parameter exactly; local justifications and objections may be omitted only when the omission and owner notification are locked.
requirements.note: The parameter is no longer forbidden in generated output when protected by historical provenance.

requirements.statement: date-création/creation-date is mandatory for all four page types.
Creation date is the date on which the page file in that language first becomes valid; it is immutable through corrections, enrichment, import and interlanguage insertion.
Publication date is stored separately in import logs.
French and English templates and parameters must never be mixed.
Generated wikicode must be complete UTF-8 and contain no explanatory comments inside page content.
Every argument page has a stable internal identifier that is the source of truth for relations, files, translations and imports.
Canonical titles are complete autonomous argumentative propositions, not themes, and are understandable outside the local branch.
Add the debate subject to a canonical title when necessary to avoid ambiguity with other pages.

Displayed titles may be shorter than canonical titles, but each remains a complete intelligible argumentative proposition with an explicit subject and predicate; a nominal topic label is insufficient.
Canonical and displayed titles must not be made identical by automation when contextual shortening is useful.
No canonical or displayed title ends with a period.
Use straight apostrophes and reject typographic apostrophes in French and English titles.
Normalize and lock every French canonical and displayed title before French page generation.
Fix and lock English canonical and displayed titles only after complete French validation.
English titles are idiomatic, autonomous, conceptually equivalent and avoid contractions when they reduce encyclopedic tone.
Locked titles can change only through an explicit migration that updates every dependent link and file.
The final logical structure is a directed acyclic graph, not merely a tree.
Distinguish nodes, edges and occurrences.
Camp and depth belong to occurrences, not to node identity.
One logical argument corresponds to one page per language even when reused in several branches or depths.
Each active node has exactly one primary occurrence; additional occurrences are secondary and do not render children.
The rendered graph root is the exact French debate title and has exactly two main branches.
Maximize coverage of important reasoning, not raw node count; exclude decorative examples, administrative details and weak reformulations as autonomous nodes.
The graph must be balanced across camps without imposing artificial numerical symmetry.
No cycles, self-relations, duplicate direct relations, duplicate direct children or unknown relations.
A child must directly justify or object to its parent rather than merely relate to the general debate.
Graph depth is unbounded; maximum observed depth is descriptive only and no warning or exceptional justification is triggered by a numeric threshold.
requirements.note: Supersedes every fixed or normal target depth.

requirements.statement: Perform an initial general documentary search before constructing the first graph.
Perform independent omission passes covering public debate and specialized literature.
Perform independent omission passes across relevant disciplinary families.
Perform an omission pass focused on actors, implementation and practical effects.
Perform an omission pass for intermediate positions, alternatives and conditional variants.
For every main argument and every crucial developed node, search explicitly for the strongest missing objection or counter-objection.
Perform a free blind-spot pass from a different research question rather than rereading the same draft.
Stop research after a documented saturation pass when new searches mostly produce duplicates, examples or marginal variants.
Consolidate semantic duplicates, choose the best hierarchy, and record every fusion, deletion and reuse decision.
Apply a deletion test: retain a node only when removing it would erase a significant distinct reasoning step.
Generate graph Markdown only from the registry/occurrences; never edit the projection independently.
In the graph rendering, reused pages are linked with MediaWiki brackets at every occurrence; unique pages are not bracketed.
Graph outputs include registry, graph JSON, graph Markdown, consolidation log, research sources and validation report.
The consolidation log records concise reasons such as duplicate, example, case-specific, wrong level, same scope or insufficient autonomy.
The research source file identifies author/institution, title, link, date when available and the argumentative families supported, without duplicating references.
Do not release graph deliverables until automated blocking validations pass and a separate semantic review covers quasi-duplicates, logic, balance and title autonomy.
sujet is the simplest general theme and is not the full interrogative debate proposition.
sujet-complet expresses the exact object and integrates naturally in a sentence rather than copying the question mechanically.
The introduction is encyclopedic, neutral, precise, substantial and normally divided into several useful subsections.

Relevant introduction topics include definitions, scope, necessary concepts, interpretations, policy variants, history, French law, European/international context, foreign experience, current debate and alternatives.
The introduction presents facts, uncertainty, interpretive disagreement, variants, implementation difficulties and relevant evolution without advocating a camp.
Do not turn the introduction into a detailed pro/con list.
Important factual claims in the introduction receive inline references; generated pages never add <references /> tags.
Verify all contemporary legal, political, scientific and statistical information on the generation date.

Do not confuse proposals with enacted law, unfinished procedures with completed ones, experiments with generalized policy, associations with causality, forecasts with facts, or recommendations with legal duties.
Use only verified existing French Wikipedia pages with exact titles, and prefer directly useful specific articles over overly general ones.
The main pro and con lists reproduce all and only primary depth-1 occurrences from the locked registry.
A reused subordinate argument appears in a main list only if it also has a primary depth-1 occurrence in the graph.
Search all nine documentary positions/categories; omit a category rather than force a weak or foreign source.
Every reference on the French Debate page, including introduction citations, is fully available in French.
requirements.note: Clarified by owner decisions and norm 1.1.4.

requirements.statement: French editions are mandatory for books when pertinent and available; general-audience web/video resources require an official French version unless an exception is documented.
requirements.note: Scientific primary literature is not excluded merely because its published language is English.

requirements.statement: Automatic subtitles, browser translation, partial/unofficial translations, French summaries or reviews do not make a foreign resource a French source.
Classify a source as pro or con only when it explicitly supports or opposes the debated proposition or a sufficiently close measure; otherwise classify it as neutral.
Do not infer support for prohibition from evidence of harm or opposition from evidence of benefit; inspect the source position rather than its title.

Avoid exact and semantic duplication across bibliography, webliography and videography; an editor page or download page does not duplicate the underlying cited publication unless it adds autonomous substantive content.
Related debates are included only when their page exists or creation is explicitly planned, and the relationship is directly thematic.
Select only central authorized sections; do not add a section solely for a secondary argument.
Debate keywords are lower-case reusable themes, normally five to eight, excluding generic action words, proposition-specific phrases and redundant synonyms.
The English Debate page is an autonomous adaptation for English-speaking or international context, not a mechanical translation of the French introduction.
It preserves the same main logical debate and primary arguments while adapting legal, political and cultural framing.
Use verified English-language references rather than reusing French-only documentary references by default.
Use only verified existing English Wikipedia pages with exact titles and direct relevance.
Apply the same epistemic cautions and neutral classification rules as the French Debate page.
Every distinct active graph node becomes exactly one French page and one English page by the end of the bilingual workflow.
Argument pages reproduce graph justifications, objections and reuses exactly; writing may enrich prose but never add, delete, merge or retype nodes.
The summary directly develops one reasoning: claim, premises, mechanism, relevance, applications, evidence and necessary limits.
Summaries are complete fluid paragraphs, not outlines or lists, and do not merely restate the title.
Indicative summary lengths are 100–160 words for simple, 150–250 for intermediate and 200–350 for complex arguments; these are quality guides, not rigid padding targets.

Use concrete examples, typical situations, mechanisms, important studies, data, historical comparisons, distinctions, practical consequences and methodological limits when they materially improve understanding.
Hypothetical examples are identified as hypothetical; important precise real cases are verified and referenced.
Do not combine several independent arguments, anticipate every objection at length, repeat the same idea, accumulate unexplained studies or describe the page externally.
Reject metadiscursive formulations such as cet argument, l'argument, this argument, cette objection or cette justification.
Treat pro and con pages with the same standards of development, evidence and methodological caution.
The French and English summaries express the same logical node and have comparable depth, but each is idiomatic rather than literal.
The English version must not be shorter, more schematic or less documented merely because it is produced second.

Argument pages use a domain-appropriate documentary profile: bibliography is generally preferred, while source hierarchy follows the nature of the reasoning and webliography or videography must add substantive value.

Prioritize the strongest sources appropriate to the field: scientific studies and syntheses, official legal materials and doctrine, primary historical sources and historiography, primary philosophical works and scholarship, official data and institutional reports, or equivalent authoritative material.
When an original study is accessible, prefer it, its DOI, journal page or official institutional report over a press article or secondary metadata page.
Every source is real, verified, directly relevant, described without exaggeration and linked to the exact claim for which it is used.
Never invent authors, titles, publication details, methods, samples, statistics, conclusions, institutions, translations or URLs.
Do not present statistical association as demonstrated causality.
Mention important limits of observational, cross-sectional, self-reported, small, old, country/platform-specific, contested or poorly generalizable studies.
A study mentioned in a summary must appear in that page's documentary parameters; documentary lists are not general reading lists.
Verify at least authors, exact title, container/work, year, volume/issue, location, publisher/institution, place, link and correspondence with the claim whenever applicable.
Preserve original titles, author names and official proper names; adapt variable dates, places and ordinary editorial wording to the page language.
French Argument pages prefer a verified French edition or equivalent whenever one exists; a foreign original requires documented absence of an equivalent or object-of-analysis status.
Inline reference calls in French prose appear before final punctuation; English prose uses the selected English convention after punctuation.
French numéro and English issue contain digits only; chapters, pages, ranges and other positions use localisation/location.

Bibliographic fields are used semantically: article for an article/chapter/contribution, ouvrage/work for the journal/book/report/container, édition/publisher for publisher and lieu/place for publication place.
HTTP/HTTPS links must be verified and point to the represented resource or authorized version.
Exact and semantic documentary duplicates are forbidden across categories and pages where they add no distinct value.
For every video, search the source page, description, credits, speakers and original publication for an author or editorially responsible entity.
Do not use a hosting platform or unofficial reposting account as author by default; prefer the official original source.
When no responsible author/entity can be identified after real verification, omit the MediaWiki author field rather than inventing one and record the checks in the source registry.
Video models never receive site or date parameters that do not exist in their official structure.
Use only the 18 authorized French rubriques and their exact official English correspondences.
Argument pages normally use one to three genuinely relevant categories, exceptionally four.

Argument keywords are two to four simple site-level navigation concepts. A keyword may occur only once in the current debate when it is central to the argument and reusable across other wiki debates; local frequency is never an admissibility criterion.
requirements.note: Owner correction 2026-07-25: reuse is evaluated at wiki scale, not debate scale.

requirements.statement: Keep established compound concepts when they function as recognized terms; otherwise split over-specific phrases into reusable concepts.
English keywords are idiomatic conceptual equivalents preserving exactly the French decreasing-relevance order.
French and English share identical active identifiers, edges, reuses and logical primary occurrences.
Different language pages may use different documentary sources when appropriate, while common sources retain identity in the source registry.
Only French pages contain interlanguage parameters; English pages never do.
French interlanguage targets come exclusively from canonical English titles locked before French page generation.
Interlanguage links are present in initial French canonical files even when English pages are created later.

The current workflow uses no interlanguage staging: canonical French files contain the links when the English translation is ready. Legacy staging is retained only for historical format compatibility.
Changing an English canonical title through migration updates the English page, all English links and all French interlanguage targets.
Adding interlanguage never changes the creation date.
One page equals one individual source file; aggregates are generated from individual files and never edited manually.
File names use stable identifiers rather than textual titles.
A coherent batch normally contains 10–25 distinct pages and follows a main argument/subgraph when possible.
Each page has exactly one owner batch per language; other batches may depend on it but may not regenerate it.
Batch reports state generated page count, identifiers, reuses, dependencies and normalization difficulties.
Every Work handoff records debate ID, versions, required state, files, SHA-256, locks, allowed outputs and prior validations.
A receiving Work rejects mismatched IDs, versions, status or hashes instead of guessing the newest file.
Aggregate separators must contain exact canonical titles and the aggregate must be deterministic.
Do not create cryptographic self-reference: archive SHA-256 belongs in an external receipt, not inside the archive it hashes.
Check remote title existence before import and classify absent, equivalent existing, collision or manual review.
Never overwrite an existing wiki page by default.
Simulation is mandatory before writing; creation uses create-only semantics.
Compare local and remote content, log differences, record revision IDs and re-read after import.
Resume logic is based on title and content SHA-256, not title alone.
Import and publication process the French Debate page before French Argument pages, then the English Debate page before English Argument pages; French interlanguage links are already included.
Historical Pywikibot tools remain read-only/non-approved until adapted to the validator, create-only, hashes and new logs.
Combine JSON Schema, semantic graph, batches, bilingual, wikicode, file/hash, workflow and report validation.
Use stable unique diagnostic codes and ERROR/WARNING/INFO severities.
Provide human-readable text and structured JSON output; blocking errors cause a non-zero exit code.
Validation mode never modifies files; recalculation/fix modes are explicit and separate.
Support whole-package and targeted validation with unit and integration tests.
Resolve local JSON Schema references using the modern referencing API rather than deprecated RefResolver architecture.
Separate machine-provable constraints, automatic documentary heuristics and editorial judgments requiring human review.
Detect duplicate identifiers/titles, dangling references, cycles, self-relations, occurrence/edge mismatch, depth/branch errors, primary occurrence errors and derived-count errors.
Detect missing/duplicate pages, batch gaps/overlaps, stale inputs, missing files, bad hashes and invalid state transitions/handoffs.
Parse wikicode to detect unknown, forbidden, empty or misordered parameters, malformed templates, wrong fixed values, mixed languages and relation mismatches.
Validate interlanguage timing, uniqueness, direction and canonical target.
Validate bilingual structural identity and report editorial asymmetries in development/documentation for human review.
Flag summary skeletons, metadiscourse, unsupported mentioned studies, missing mechanisms and camp imbalance as heuristic or human-review findings rather than pretending full semantic proof.
Do not release any Work stage with unresolved blocking errors; failure still produces a report and blocked handoff.
A debate closes only after French, English, bilingual, interlanguage, import and release validations succeed.
The final package is autonomous outside conversations and contains manifests, registry, graph, pages, reports, patches and logs.
After verification, move all debate conversations and final artifacts to the archive project and remove debate-specific temporary files from the active project.
Retain every empty parameter in generated Debate pages.
requirements.note: Replaced by omission of optional empty parameters.

requirements.statement: Former rule grouping Débat construit with Généré par IA.
requirements.note: Partially restored for avancement only; AI warning wording remains governed by MW-007.

requirements.statement: Limit every graph to level 3 and forbid level 4.
requirements.note: Replaced by normal target 3 with justified levels 4–5.

requirements.statement: Lock canonical English titles before French page generation while deferring English page content.
requirements.note: Reactivated in a limited form by norm 1.2.0 to support direct interlanguage links.

requirements.statement: Insert interlanguage links in the initial valid generation of every French page.
requirements.note: Reactivated by norm 1.2.0; late staging is historical only.

requirements.statement: Produce French and English Argument pages in a single monolithic Work.
requirements.note: Replaced by separate sequential French and English Work.

requirements.statement: Require every video author field to be filled regardless of verifiability.
requirements.note: Systematic search remains mandatory; verified absence is exceptionally represented by omission plus registry note.

requirements.statement: After passes A–F, repeat complete saturation passes until two consecutive passes find no important distinct argument; perform at most six additional saturation passes and report the limit if important additions still occur.

After pruning, conduct a final independent omission pass over main arguments, strongest reasons and objections, intermediate positions, alternatives, affected actors, implementation, indirect and long-term effects; any important addition restarts consolidation on the affected branch.
A debate, cross-interview, round table or parliamentary hearing presenting several positions is neutral videography; a pro/con video requires an explicit identifiable position.
Do not duplicate the same video in several documentary positions and prefer a stable official source over an unidentified social repost.

For a French translation or edition, use the verified French title, publisher, publication date and direct French link; distinguish correctly article/chapter, containing work, authoring institution and publisher.
After each batch, report page count, identifiers, reused pages and material normalization difficulties without placing commentary inside wikicode.
When title and scope are sufficiently clear, execute each Work autonomously without requesting intermediate validation or confirmation.
Infer minor missing scope details from the natural reading of the title; report only ambiguities that could materially alter the output.
Do not expose intermediate graph drafts; complete research, enrichment, consolidation, pruning and validation before delivering final graph files.
Final page-generation outputs contain complete wikicode without ellipses, placeholders or abridged sections.
The final French Debate Work returns only a brief verification statement and the complete MediaWiki page artifact, not an additional page summary.
Argument Work makes reasonable editorial decisions but records choices that could change the meaning of a node.
Graph research uses Web sources when the subject requires current or external verification and represents several serious positions.
Do not continue research indefinitely; stop according to the saturation criterion and disclose residual research limitations.
As a non-binding coverage guide, aim normally for roughly six to ten main arguments per camp; never create or keep nodes merely to reach a quota.

As a non-binding guide, a main argument normally receives two to five direct justifications and two to five direct objections; fewer are preferable when further children would be weak, redundant or remote.

A developed crucial node normally receives two to four strong justifications and objections without mechanical quotas; deeper levels 4 or 5 are used only where the discussion is central and requires them.

Initial framing explicitly maps the evaluated proposition, important variants, affected actors, institutions, professionals, beneficiaries, third parties, indirect effects, relevant disciplines and material scope ambiguities.

A candidate node is autonomous only when it is a complete contestable proposition, adds a distinct premise, mechanism, objection or consequence, matters to serious debate, can sustain a substantive page and would leave a real gap if removed; examples and narrow administrative details remain examples.
Graph titles state the central reason directly, avoid metadiscourse and simple themes, and do not mechanically repeat the overall debate conclusion in every node.

Logical review distinguishes principle from application, rule from example, cause from consequence, empirical finding from normative conclusion, legal from moral reasoning, economic from social reasoning, existence from feasibility of an alternative, and transition possibility from transition cost.

Strong-objection passes test premises, mechanisms, logical links, scope, proportionality, empirical validity, legal validity, practical implementation and less costly or less restrictive alternatives whenever relevant.

Graph research prioritizes official legal and institutional sources, scientific and academic publications, directly relevant professional or association reports, authoritative books and quality press for documented public positions, while representing several serious positions and verifying current facts.

The ASCII rendering contains only the debate title, camp labels, argument titles, Justifications/Objections labels and reuse brackets; it contains no IDs, level numbers, notes, summaries, references, categories, keywords, JSON or working comments.
The graph Markdown contains, in order, the title, complete ASCII graph, recap table, reused-page table, concise pass note, final-control note and residual scope/research limits.

The recap table reports main pro/con arguments, justifications and objections by depth, distinct pages, total occurrences, reused pages, additional reuses, developed pages and pages used only as secondary links; every value is recalculated from the registry.
The reused-page table reports canonical page, occurrence count, full-development location and other use locations, exactly matching occurrences and the unique primary occurrence.
The validation report lists executed checks, numerical results, corrected anomalies and each final result, and uses VALIDATION GLOBALE : RÉUSSIE only when no blocking error remains.

The consolidation log records completed passes and added, removed, merged, renamed, moved, reused and converted-to-example items, stop condition and residual limits, using concise editorial reasons rather than private reasoning.
Research sources record title, author or institution, date when available, link, verification role and pro/con/neutral status without forcing a position or duplicating documentary records.
The rendered tree has no orphan line, uses the correct box-drawing connectors and visually attaches every item to its actual parent.
A title may not reappear within its own descendant subgraph, and a node may not combine independent reasonings merely for convenience.

Inline introduction references specifically cover laws and bills, judicial decisions, historical dates, statistics, study results, foreign experiences, public policies, institutional statements and legislative-procedure status whenever these claims are material.
Wikipedia title verification includes accents, capitalization, disambiguation parentheses, singular/plural and the exact existing title; inventing or approximating a page title is forbidden.

Argument page links use the exact locked canonical title; displayed titles may omit redundant context but remain complete, faithful and intelligible argumentative sentences, never nominal labels and never replacements for the canonical page field.

Bibliography contains books, chapters, scientific or academic articles, reports and other publication-like works; webliography contains autonomous substantive web resources rather than mere catalogue, sales, announcement, download or summary pages for publications already cited.

A bibliographic and a web reference to the same underlying work coexist only when the web page has independent substantial content and that distinct contribution is recorded; otherwise retain the primary publication.
Do not duplicate a cited publication through an editor or bookseller page, release announcement, press article announcing it, press release or news page merely summarizing the same report or study.
A related debate is not merely a shared theme, an argument or a Wikipedia article; it is a distinct debate page with a direct thematic relationship.
If no sufficiently relevant verified French Wikipedia article, documentary source or related debate exists, omit the optional parameter rather than inventing, translating or weakening the criterion.
The French Debate Work performs a final structural, source, language, classification, duplicate, Wikipedia, graph-link, current-fact, interlanguage-timing and creation-date checklist before delivery.
Each Argument page is informative and understandable independently of the graph, while remaining exactly one logical node.

A coherent batch preferably contains a main argument, its direct justifications and objections, lower dependent nodes and unproduced reused pages assigned to that owner batch, with dependencies declared rather than duplicated.
Before page writing, extract all distinct node IDs, count occurrences, distinct pages, reuses, main arguments, justifications and objections, and report structural inconsistencies.

Study evidence is used to confirm a mechanism, give an order of magnitude, show group variation, test a hypothesis, reveal a limit or provide a documented example, and its relevance is explained rather than merely cited.
Do not overload Argument pages with redundant references or unexplained study lists; every documentary item supports a statement actually made in that page.
Individual page files and aggregate page records remain clearly separated, syntactically complete and compatible with automated import; no explanatory commentary appears inside wikicode.
The independent registry/JSON source stores IDs and relations separately from wikicode so pages and aggregates can be regenerated deterministically.
French and English page sets undergo structural, title, wikicode, linguistic-reference and summary-quality checks, including broken links, self-relations, direct-child duplicates and camp parity.
Canonical English titles are locked before French generation solely for direct interlanguage targets; English prose and documentation are not produced until French validation is complete.
French descriptive dates use natural French order and month names; English descriptive dates use natural English forms, while exact source titles remain unchanged.
Use the established French or English form of a publication place when one exists, and do not artificially translate place names normally retained unchanged.

For translated or language-specific editions, link directly to the represented edition and use that edition’s verified title, publisher or broadcaster and date rather than metadata from another language version.
A bilingual resource counts for a language only when the complete relevant content is actually available in that language; an abstract, partial excerpt or review is insufficient.
When no individual video author is identifiable, use a verified media outlet, programme, institution or official editorial channel only if it is genuinely responsible for the content.
A missing video author remains exceptional and is accepted only after checking the page, description, credits, speakers and original source; the registry records those checks.

The mandatory graph deliverables are graph/graphe_argumentatif.md, graph/graphe_argumentatif.json, graph/validation_report.txt, graph/consolidation_log.json and graph/research_sources.md, plus the master registry and handoffs required by the workflow.
Graph, page and aggregate outputs contain no ellipses or omitted branches; all mandatory artifacts are complete.
A Work output report lists produced paths, main counts, validation status and material residual limits without duplicating full artifacts in the conversation when files have been created.
Every aggregate page separator uses the exact locked canonical title and every page appears once; the individual files remain authoritative over aggregates.

The graph Work final response states completion, gives the five artifact paths, summarizes main counts, reports global validation and mentions only important residual limits; it does not paste the whole graph when the file exists.
Do not expose private detailed reasoning; logs contain only concise verifiable editorial operations and reasons.
Never claim that a search, pass, source verification or validation was performed unless it was actually executed on the current inputs.
Numerical ranges are coverage guides only; never invent nodes, references or prose to satisfy a quota.
Do not edit derived counts, graph projections or aggregate files manually; update the source registry and regenerate.
Do not deliver competing graph versions, incomplete branches, placeholders or points of suspension as final artifacts.
When a category has no qualifying source, omit it and disclose the absence where operationally useful instead of weakening language, relevance or verification requirements.
For sufficiently clear large graphs, report structural counts and material ambiguities through files/reports rather than interrupting autonomous batch production for unnecessary confirmation.
Use a node model where camp and level are intrinsic fields of each node rather than occurrence properties.
requirements.note: Replaced by nodes/edges/occurrences DAG model.

requirements.statement: Generate Argument pages without mandatory AI-warning and creation-date fields.
requirements.note: Mandatory warnings and creation dates were added later.

requirements.statement: Limit Argument documentary parameters to bibliography only.
requirements.note: Domain-appropriate documentary profile prefers bibliography but permits web/video sources when substantively necessary.

requirements.statement: Use the original aggregate-only pages.wiki/pages.json layout as the authoritative storage format.
requirements.note: Replaced by one individual source file per page plus generated aggregates.

requirements.statement: Treat date-création or creation-date as the immediate draft-generation date even before validation.
requirements.note: Refined to the date on which the language-specific page file first becomes valid.

requirements.statement: Keep warning parameters and nested warnings present even when empty.
requirements.note: Allowed structurally but not generated; empty optional parameters are omitted.

requirements.statement: Argument summaries defend the strongest sourced version of the node and contain no self-objection, weakening final concession, or metadiscourse.
Pure bibliographic pagination is stored in page as digits or a hyphenated range; location/localisation is reserved for non-page locators.
Web date contains a verified publication or substantive update date, never an access date; it is omitted when unverifiable.
French pages cite a verified French edition of a book when a pertinent edition exists, without artificially translating scientific article titles.
Displayed titles are reviewed individually and may not be mechanically copied across the entire corpus.
Categories/sections and keywords are assigned individually and mechanically uniform distributions are blocked.
Debate pages use substantive introductions and non-quota documentary distributions covering the principal dimensions of the controversy.
Corpus-specific creation dates are declared in a local profile or manifest and never hard-coded in the generic norm, validator or publication kit.
requirements.note: Corpus-specific historical decisions remain only in archived provenance documents and in the corpus packages concerned.

requirements.statement: Corrective work uses corrective_in_progress/corrective_blocked and returns to release_ready only after full validation, without rewriting historical handoffs.
No W10 corrective revision performs remote writes; the aligned W11 kit is included separately, non-executed, and validates public-template compatibility before any write.
Validation is strictly read-only and every new binary corrective rule has positive and negative test coverage where applicable.
French and English canonical/displayed titles use straight ASCII double quotes; typographic or angle quotation marks are forbidden in page names.
requirements.note: Keyboard-accessibility rule.

requirements.statement: Important factual claims in every English introduction subsection receive inline references; generated pages never add <references /> tags.
Exactly one consolidated norm is active at normative root; older consolidated norms are stored only in history.
Existing pages are never overwritten by default; equivalent content is skipped and differing content is classified as a collision requiring manual review.
Every successful write is re-read, content-hash verified and logged with its revision ID.
Resume logic uses title, expected content SHA-256 and verified remote revision state.
User-test and publication load the exact signed simulation plan from disk; they never rebuild it silently.
The signed plan includes and rechecks fingerprints of manifest, release manifest and validator before any write.
Resume planning accepts a French page already identical to the final interlanguage content instead of reporting a false collision.
Every displayed title has a page-level review decision; no global identity quota substitutes for review.
Every selected rubric is reviewed page by page and has its own rationale; no rubric receives special treatment.
The review ledger rationale keys exactly match the selected rubrics for every active node.
Corpus-specific dates, report paths, Work identifiers and handoffs are package-declared and absent from generic runtime code.
Argument summaries use a general-public encyclopedic style and state the central claim at the beginning rather than building a long academic introduction.
Summaries vary sentence length and avoid a sequence of long, heavily subordinated sentences; automated sentence-length signals are warnings, not proof of poor style.
Scientific, technical, legal and philosophical terms needed by the reasoning are briefly defined at their first meaningful occurrence for a non-specialist reader.
requirements.note: The rule applies generically to any specialized term that a non-specialist reader cannot reasonably be expected to know.

requirements.statement: Definitions are integrated into the explanation and do not turn the summary into a glossary; common-language terms are not defined artificially.
Names of researchers, studies and methods appear only when useful and normally after the idea they document has been explained in accessible language.
A page-level human review attests thesis-first structure, general-public accessibility, sentence rhythm and treatment of necessary technical terms for every produced language.

The opening sentence develops the argument beyond the canonical or displayed title by introducing a concrete phenomenon, decisive premise, causal mechanism, consequence or useful distinction; a close restatement of the title is insufficient.
requirements.note: Automated title-opening similarity is heuristic and cannot replace page-level review.

requirements.statement: Concrete examples, orders of magnitude and quantitative data are used only when they materially improve understanding or demonstration; their presence is never a quota or mandatory decoration.
Every quantitative claim in a summary is supported by documentary material on the page and human-reviewed for population, scope, date and context; artificial precision is prohibited.
requirements.note: The validator can detect many digit-based claims but cannot establish substantive source support on its own.

requirements.statement: A summary may use a firm, vivid and mildly biting formulation to convey the force of the reasoning, while avoiding sarcasm, militancy, contempt, caricature, unsupported certainty and mechanically repeated slogans.

The page-level bilingual review records explicit decisions on title development, example-or-data relevance, quantitative verification when applicable, assertive tone and absence of polemical overstatement.
A canonical title is referentially autonomous: contextual demonstratives and pronouns require an antecedent inside the title; a displayed title may rely on an unambiguous immediate context.
All French pages, including the Debate page, use the Lien interlangue subtemplate from their first valid generation.
English Debate pages use topic and complete-topic and never use type.
Generated pages never contain references tags; inline ref calls remain allowed and required where applicable.
French Debate references, including inline introduction calls, are entirely available in French.
Argument pages use a verified equivalent in the page language whenever one exists; cross-language use is explicitly justified.
Debate bibliography contains foundational books or broad syntheses rather than narrow argument-level studies.
Web authors are emitted only after attribution verification, and page is omitted when identical to site.
Generated French prose uses parentheses, not paired em dashes, for parenthetical asides, appositions and inserted enumerations.
Package SHA-256 manifests are exhaustive; declared file, requirement and test counts equal the delivered artifacts.

Canonical publication begins by creating and verifying the canonical French Debate page from the signed plan; a signed debate-test receipt is remotely reverified before any remaining write, and no user-space test page is created.
Publication configurations for page content run every applicable validation scope, including wikicode and editorial.
Active examples and checklists include direct French interlanguage links and contain no late-staging instruction.
A bilingual introduction-review ledger records every actual subsection title, its purpose and why it is necessary for understanding the debate.
A technical or specialized subsection is retained only when its relevance to the debated question is explained explicitly.
The introduction follows a coherent progression for a non-specialist reader, and each subsection title and opening make its role clear.
No universal minimum of five subsections or twenty references applies; any local minimum is justified by the breadth and complexity of the debate.
Generic introduction rules contain no topic-specific checklist, corpus identifier or pilot-debate constant.
The introduction states the stakes of the debate explicitly rather than leaving them implicit in the argument tree.
The validator requires and checks the bilingual introduction-review ledger against the actual subsection titles for every corpus processed by the current components.
The self-audit of generic components searches active rules, examples, code and configurations for pilot-corpus identifiers and topic-specific constants outside explicitly historical paths.
Introduction writing starts from the reader's comprehension needs, not from argument-tree branches or documentary source families.
Debate-specific publication configurations remain in the debate corpus and are not distributed inside the generic publication kit.
Inline references in debate introductions are driven by factual claims requiring attribution; no global or per-subsection minimum applies.

The validator does not require at least one inline reference call; it checks forbidden references tags, control activation and human review consistency for every corpus processed by the current components.
French rubriques and English sections are alphabetized independently in their own language; bilingual equivalence compares conceptual sets rather than list positions.
The French sujet and English topic values begin with a capital letter.
French sujet-complet and English complete-topic are non-interrogative complements that fit the headings Arguments pour et contre… and Pros and cons of… naturally.
For Debate-page rubriques and sections, precision takes precedence over exhaustiveness; only categories central to the controversy as a whole are retained.
Debate-page documentation is proportionate to the abundance of the literature, and bibliography, webliography and videography are reviewed separately without a universal quota.
Each language-level summary review records an exact expression present in the summary that makes its firm, vivid or mildly biting force perceptible.
The validator checks alphabetical rubrique/section order and the initial capital in sujet/topic for every corpus processed by the current components.
The validator checks complete-topic heading fit heuristics, debate classification/documentation attestations, and that each forceful-expression excerpt occurs in the corresponding summary.
Complete documentary dates are written in natural language in the page language; ISO machine dates are forbidden, while creation dates remain YYYY-MM-DD.
requirements.note: Bare years remain valid when only the year is known.

requirements.statement: Inline introduction citations are written directly as readable wikicode inside ref tags; no MediaWiki citation template is used in French or English.
requirements.note: Named references are permitted when their first definition contains direct textual wikicode; self-closing reuse remains allowed.

requirements.statement: Each of the nine documentary parameters on every French Débat and English Debate page contains at least two distinct references.
When a subject has a common acronym, it is declared in the review ledger and used in sujet-complet or complete-topic.
requirements.note: The ledger records null when no common acronym applies.

requirements.statement: Adjacent MediaWiki templates are concatenated as }}{{ without any intervening line break or whitespace in generated French and English page wikicode.
requirements.note: The forbidden form includes one or more LF or CRLF line breaks, with optional horizontal whitespace, between }} and {{. The canonical replacement is }}{{.

requirements.statement: French pages may be published before English pages exist in the page manifest when future English canonical titles are locked in the master registry and match the French interlanguage targets.

A debate archive can be extracted, validated, planned, tested, published and archived through one portable command, without requiring a release_ready filename suffix, with canonical scopes all, fr, en, fr-debate and en-debate.
Within each language, the Debate page is always processed before all Argument pages; a configuration requesting the reverse order is rejected.
Pywikibot credentials are stored only under private/pywikibot, while private, corpus, archives, updates, incoming, logs, plans, state and virtual-environment directories are excluded from Git.
No persistent file in the installation stores the absolute path of the project root; configurations, reports, plans and logs use portable relative paths or identifiers.
A one-command component update validates and tests staged packages, archives previous components and incoming archives, atomically installs the new versions and leaves updates empty after success.
The portable source tree is versioned in Git and pushed to the configured GitHub origin after successful updates, while runtime data and secrets remain untracked.
Debate ZIP archives are placed directly in incoming; one ZIP is selected automatically regardless of its filename, while multiple ZIPs require a selector matching exactly the chosen filename stem.
A debate archive filename is only a file selector and need not match manifest.debate_id; the internal debate_id is authoritative for corpus identity.

Publication executes the currently installed validator and requires its exact runtime version and a positive report, while corpus normative_versions remain immutable historical provenance and need not equal installed component versions when the declared norm is compatible.

The last effectively published state is preserved and signed for each debate and language, with page identity, canonical title, content hash, MediaWiki revision, status, receipt, publication date and corpus version.
A reprise classifies every page exactly once as create, skip, update, move, redirect, delete, manual_review or blocked.
Retired pages are computed from a signed prior published state minus the new corpus; absence from the new manifest alone never proves eligibility for deletion.
A remote update is automatic only when prior ownership and the expected published revision or hash are verified and MediaWiki concurrency controls prevent an intervening overwrite.
A human or indeterminate remote modification is never overwritten automatically and is reported as manual_review with old, remote and proposed comparisons.
Deletion requires prior ownership, absence from the new corpus, no known cross-debate reuse, unchanged expected revision or hash, Wikidéb’IA markers and the effective delete right.
A deletion is never silently replaced by a deletion-request banner; an unsafe deletion is blocked or sent to manual_review.
A stable logical identity with a changed canonical title produces a move, while a merge declares its target, incoming links and an explicit redirect-or-delete policy.
The remote operation plan is deterministic, signed and locked before writes and records preconditions, expected revisions, hashes, justifications and execution results.
Creates and updates precede moves and redirects, the published graph is verified before final deletions, and a failure before that gate prevents deletion.
Remote operations are idempotent and restart-safe, recognizing already completed actions and blocking pages that changed after planning.
The update command supports language scopes, dry-run, no-delete and only-delete; component replacement is exposed under the distinct upgrade command.
Effective edit, createpage, move and delete rights are checked for all selected languages before the first write; missing delete stops a deletion scope without interactive fallback.
French and English authentication reuse the private wikidebates BotPassword configuration and are processed sequentially with controlled error logging.
The validator checks remote plan schemas, signatures, counts, unique mutating targets, update preconditions, deletion safety and manual-review comparison links while remaining local and read-only.
JSON Schemas are provided for published states, migration declarations, remote update plans and final remote receipts.
No secret, absolute installation path, corpus-specific constant or interactive Pywikibot prompt is introduced by the update workflow.
Every generated Debate page contains a non-empty Wikipedia-article parameter with at least one exact, verified article title in the page language.

New Debate pages normally omit débats-connexes/related-debates; during FR→EN translation, related-debates contains only French source relations whose English counterpart page is verified to exist, and no relation absent from the French source is added.
requirements.note: FR→EN translation is the explicit exception to the ordinary new-page omission rule.

requirements.statement: JSON author arrays are converted to MediaWiki text: one item becomes a scalar, multiple items are separated by a comma followed by a space, and an empty list omits the parameter.
The publish command runs without an interactive yes/no prompt; the orchestrator automatically passes the signed plan hash to the execution engine after validation.

When several authors are rendered in auteurs or authors, the canonical separator is exactly a comma followed by one space; semicolons, fullwidth commas and malformed comma spacing are forbidden in generated output.
Every displayed title states the argumentative claim as a complete proposition; immediate context may shorten redundant framing but cannot supply a missing predicate, conclusion or logical relation.
requirements.note: Titles still omit a final period. The automatic check is conservative and the page-level bilingual review remains mandatory.

requirements.statement: Displayed titles must fulfil a genuinely concise reading function: exact identity with the canonical title is exceptional, individually justified in each language, and limited to at most 10 percent of active arguments per language.
requirements.note: The rule prevents displayed_title from becoming a mechanical duplicate of the page name while preserving complete propositional wording.

requirements.statement: The validator rejects obviously nominal displayed titles and requires page-level bilingual attestations that each displayed title is a complete intelligible proposition.
requirements.note: Implemented by WDV-EDT-021 in validator 0.4.21.

requirements.statement: The validator requires graph_placement_review_path and blocks incomplete coverage, divergent occurrence metadata, incompatible semantic targets or functions, failed main-argument tests and unapproved parent fit.
The validator blocks a displayed-title copy ratio above 10 percent per language and requires concision attestations plus a non-empty node-specific justification for every retained exact identity.
requirements.note: Implemented by WDV-EDT-001 and WDV-EDT-012 in validator 0.4.24.

requirements.statement: A depth-1 occurrence is a main argument only when it directly answers the debate proposition, remains autonomous without an implicit parent, organizes a distinct argument family and has no preferable more general non-duplicate parent.

A targeted objection, secondary proof, historical or scientific example, particular interpretation, doctrinal instantiation, technical mechanism or sectoral application is subordinate to the argument it primarily supports, attacks or specifies unless it independently passes every main-argument test.

A graph-placement review covers every active occurrence, records its semantic target and final function, and gives strengthened attestations for main arguments and direct-parent attestations for subordinate occurrences.

sujet and topic use the most concise conventional nominal label available, such as a noun phrase, doctrine name or established -ism, rather than a descriptive paraphrase when an accurate concept label exists.

sujet-complet and complete-topic normally begin with a lowercase alphabetic character in both languages because they complete an already-started heading; an unavoidable proper-name or acronym exception is individually justified.

Webliographic and videographic metadata de-duplication applies to Debate and Argument pages alike. page/title equal to site is omitted; author equal to site triggers a renewed authorship search and, if no distinct responsibility is found, the author field is omitted.
requirements.note: Implemented under WDV-DOC-004.

requirements.statement: Remote corpus updates use the concise default edit summary Corrections and do not expose debate identifiers, manifest hashes or internal corpus versions in ordinary wiki history.

A single complete delivery ZIP remains directly installable: it exposes all three component ZIPs at its root for legacy managers, while the current manager can additionally discover them through one nested bundle.

The validator checks lowercase complete-topic initials, required nominal-topic review attestations, authorship re-check attestations for web/video sources, and author-site or page-site metadata collisions on every generated page type.
requirements.note: Uses WDV-EDT-018 and WDV-DOC-004.

requirements.statement: In argument summaries, a specialized notion is made understandable at its first useful occurrence either by a concise in-prose explanation or by the localized Wikipedia hover template when the corresponding article lead is sufficient; the template never replaces the argument mechanism or documentary support.

French introduction prose may use {{Lien Wikipédia|article=…}} at the first useful occurrence of a genuinely specialized notion; texte-affiché is used only for a real wording difference, while initial lowercase adaptation is made directly in article.
English introduction prose uses {{Wikipedia link|article=…}} and the optional displayed-text parameter under the same first-occurrence, language-verification and non-documentary rules as French.

Inline explanatory templates are restricted to Lien Wikipédia(article, optional texte-affiché) in French and Wikipedia link(article, optional displayed-text) in English, within introduction content and argument summaries only; article is required and the templates are forbidden inside ref notes.

Drafting instructions identify only notions whose explanation would materially help a non-specialist, link the first useful occurrence, avoid repeated or decorative linking, and retain a prose explanation whenever the Wikipedia lead is insufficient or the concept is central to the reasoning.

The validator checks localized Wikipedia hover template names and parameters, requires a non-empty article, rejects redundant display parameters and links inside ref notes, and requires introduction and summary review attestations for link-or-definition treatment.
requirements.note: Implemented by WDV-MWK-020 and WDV-EDT-013/017 in validator 0.4.26.

requirements.statement: A signed published state is written only after executable operations have been applied and verified, or after a complete signed no_changes attestation; unresolved plans never replace the prior state.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — safe remote update execution

requirements.statement: Generic norm, validator, kit and complete-component bundle archives contain no debate corpus; debate corpora are separate artifacts unless explicitly requested.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — safe remote update execution

requirements.statement: Any blocked or manual_review operation prevents execution before the first write and prevents success receipts and published-state replacement.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — safe remote update execution
requirements.note: Enforced independently by the manager and signed-plan executor.

requirements.statement: A plan containing only skip operations performs no MediaWiki write but is remotely reread and recorded through a signed no_changes attestation that refreshes the published state with exact current revisions.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — safe remote update execution
requirements.note: The attestation is blocked by any divergence after planning.

requirements.statement: An update dry-run never changes corpus/; archive inputs are extracted to staging and promoted only after a real successful or no_changes run with no unresolved operation.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — safe remote update execution

requirements.statement: update <debate_id> uses only the installed corpus; every archive is selected explicitly with --archive, with no fallback from an absent installed ID or a lone incoming ZIP.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — safe remote update execution

requirements.statement: The component test and delivery gates cover manual-review blocking, all-skip false-success prevention, installed-corpus priority, archive staging, dry-run immutability and absence of debate corpora from generic deliveries.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — safe remote update execution
requirements.note: Implemented by kit 2.2.13 tests and release integrity checks; 1.2.26 supersedes the all-skip detail of 1.2.25.

requirements.statement: A no_changes published state is a signed remote attestation, not a mutation receipt: every active page is reread and matched exactly before state renewal.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — no-change attestation and deferred scopes

requirements.statement: Archive selection for remote update is accepted only through --archive; absent installed corpora and lone incoming archives never trigger an implicit fallback.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — no-change attestation and deferred scopes

requirements.statement: Every update staging directory is removed after dry-run, unresolved plan, no_changes attestation, success or failure; promotion occurs only after verified completion.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — no-change attestation and deferred scopes

requirements.statement: When mutable operations exist but none belongs to the requested scope, update returns no_changes_in_scope, performs no execution and does not promote a staged corpus.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — no-change attestation and deferred scopes

requirements.statement: A --no-delete run preserves verified removed pages as pending_delete in the signed state so a later --only-delete run retains ownership and deletion preconditions.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — no-change attestation and deferred scopes

requirements.statement: Release tests cover signed no_changes state refresh, post-plan divergence rejection, strict archive selection, staging cleanup, scope-aware no-op handling and deferred deletion continuity.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-02 — no-change attestation and deferred scopes
requirements.note: Implemented by kit 2.2.13 regression tests.

requirements.statement: The final bilingual pages are rendered deterministically only from sealed graph, metadata, content and translation locks.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-03 — bilingual rendering and interlanguage links
requirements.note: Implemented by kit 2.10.0.

requirements.statement: French pages require exactly one interlanguage link only when English translation is ready or published; deferred French pages omit it.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-03 — bilingual rendering and interlanguage links
requirements.note: The unconditional immediate-link rule is replaced by norm 1.2.34.

requirements.statement: During English projection, the French Citation model becomes the English Quote model and all template parameter names use the declared English contract. Only the values of quote (from citation) and date are translated; every other documentary value and the parameter order are preserved exactly.
requirements.note: English parameter names are mandatory: citation→quote, auteurs→authors, ouvrage→work, numéro→issue, localisation→location, édition→publisher, lieu→place, lien→link, avertissements-citation→warnings.

requirements.statement: The translated English Quote receives AI-translated quote in warnings, appended once with the canonical separator comma-space when another warning exists.
requirements.note: Duplicate warning insertion is forbidden.

requirements.statement: Every generated English page uses only English model names and English parameter names, including nested models; every generated French page uses the corresponding French contract.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-04 — complete localization of English wikicode
requirements.note: French templates or parameter names in English introduction, summaries, relations, references or quotes are blocking.

requirements.statement: Graph depth is unbounded: no normal target, declared maximum or numeric warning threshold is applied; maximum_observed is descriptive and parent-child depth consistency remains mandatory.

Common-noun keywords use lowercase canonical spelling; uppercase spelling is reserved for justified proper names, official names, brands, acronyms and initialisms. Case-only duplicate vocabulary entries are forbidden in both languages.
requirements.note: Examples: revenu is lowercase; Dieu and ONU retain canonical capitals.

requirements.statement: An Argument-page reference is selected because it develops or supports that argument; also discussing objections is permitted and never a removal criterion once argument development is verified.
requirements.note: Context-only or objection-only material does not qualify as an Argument reference.

requirements.statement: A package may explicitly declare translation_status.en=deferred to publish French pages before English translation, without English titles, English page manifests or French interlanguage links.
English publication scopes are blocked while translation_status.en is deferred.
Locked, ready or published English states remain strict: missing canonical titles, empty or mismatched interlanguage targets and incomplete English pages are blocking.
Leaving deferred for ready or published re-enables bilingual controls and permits a later French update that adds exact interlanguage links without changing creation dates.

An explicit deferred English translation status is an operational workflow declaration and may be applied to a supported historical corpus without migrating its provenance revision; the current editorial rules still apply cumulatively.
requirements.note: Absence of the explicit declaration remains strict.

requirements.statement: Imported or resumed corpora may preserve immutable creation dates page by page when the manifest, canonical wikicode and registry agree exactly.
A legacy displayed-title identity exception must be owner-locked, file-backed, exhaustive and limited to already locked exact identities; the normal ratio remains strict for every non-exempt node.
requirements.note: Remplacé par la révision 1.2.42 : aucune proportion minimale de titres affichés distincts n’est exigée.

requirements.statement: Argument keywords name atomic navigation concepts. Productive mini-headings such as “limites de la science”, “histoire des religions” and “construction des lois scientifiques” are rejected when a simple concept exists.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-05 — atomic keywords and summary originality
requirements.note: Lexicalized expressions remain possible only through a page-specific controlled-vocabulary exception.

requirements.statement: A keyword must be a semantic navigation atom. Transparent intersections of domains are decomposed into base keywords; lexicalized categories such as 'argument d’autorité' remain whole. Entries attest atomic_concept=true and compositional_intersection=false.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-05 — atomic keywords and summary originality
requirements.note: “lois de la nature” is a compliant example when the exception is documented.

requirements.statement: Argument summaries explain the node-specific mechanism and may not consist of generic scaffolding, metadiscourse or an enumeration of linked justification and objection titles.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-05 — atomic keywords and summary originality

requirements.statement: The validator blocks known summary scaffolds, two-or-more copied child titles, and any normalized sentence of at least eight words repeated in four or more summaries of the same corpus.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-05 — atomic keywords and summary originality

requirements.statement: Each summary review attests originality and embeds a mechanism_statement excerpt actually present in the summary; French summaries also use “Dieu” as a proper name except in genuinely generic common-noun uses.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-05 — atomic keywords and summary originality

requirements.statement: Transparent intersections of disciplines or themes are decomposed into independently clickable base keywords in French and English; adjectival paraphrase does not make the expression atomic.
requirements.note: ‘psychologie religieuse’ becomes ‘psychologie’ and ‘religion’, while ‘argument d'autorité’ remains a lexicalized atomic category.

requirements.statement: Une correction ciblée ne modifie pas les résumés historiques sans décision explicite du propriétaire; leur empreinte est vérifiée par un verrou machine.
Le paramètre initialisation/initialization historique est conservé exactement lorsqu’il est attesté; il reste interdit sur une page nouvelle.

Une même référence ne figure jamais dans plusieurs orientations documentaires de la page Débat. Une source qui expose substantiellement les arguments pour et contre est classée uniquement dans la documentation neutre.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-06 — documentation, introduction and displayed titles
requirements.note: Aucun quota minimal ne s’applique à un paramètre documentaire individuel.

requirements.statement: Toute référence vidéographique YouTube indique le créateur ou la chaîne lorsque cette attribution est visible sur la plateforme.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-06 — documentation, introduction and displayed titles

requirements.statement: L’introduction est structurée selon les informations réellement nécessaires au lecteur. Les sous-parties génériques, redondantes ou limitées à annoncer des enjeux sans information propre sont supprimées.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-06 — documentation, introduction and displayed titles
requirements.note: Remplacé par EDT-061 et la révision 1.2.43 : la rubrique d’enjeux est obligatoire, mais doit rester concrète et non redondante.

requirements.statement: Le titre canonique peut être repris à l’identique comme titre affiché sans quota ni justification d’exception lorsqu’il est déjà clair, complet et lisible.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-06 — documentation, introduction and displayed titles

requirements.statement: Un titre affiché distinct n’est retenu que si la revue atteste une amélioration réelle de lisibilité et une équivalence sémantique exacte avec le titre canonique; la seule réduction de longueur ne suffit pas.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-06 — documentation, introduction and displayed titles

requirements.statement: Toute introduction comporte une sous-partie dédiée intitulée « Enjeux du débat » en français ou « Stakes of the debate » en anglais. Elle développe au moins deux conséquences concrètes propres au sujet, sans reproduire le graphe argumentatif ni énumérer des domaines abstraits.
requirements.note: La présence du titre est automatique; la concrétisation et la non-redondance sont attestées dans la revue.

requirements.statement: Une simple notice documentaire placée dans <ref> ne reçoit aucun point final avant </ref>; un point interne est réservé à une phrase explicative complète et doit être attesté par SHA-256 dans la revue.
requirements.note: La ponctuation de la phrase principale est placée après l’appel de note.

requirements.statement: Les notions spécialisées de même rang énumérées dans un même passage reçoivent un traitement cohérent par les liens Wikipédia explicatifs; toute asymétrie est justifiée notion par notion.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-06 — local consistency of Wikipedia hover links
requirements.note: La règle porte sur la cohérence locale, sans quota global de liens.

requirements.statement: Le validateur vérifie le registre des groupes de notions et la présence réelle des liens déclarés dans chaque sous-partie, indépendamment de toute métadonnée de révision de politique.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-06 — local consistency of Wikipedia hover links

requirements.statement: Chaque sous-partie d’introduction possède un inventaire exhaustif des notions spécialisées, chacune liée, expliquée, rattachée à un traitement antérieur ou explicitement jugée claire en contexte.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-06 — exhaustive review of complex notions in introductions
requirements.note: Cette exigence remplace le mécanisme principal fondé sur les seuls groupes de notions voisines.

requirements.statement: Le validateur contrôle l’inventaire de chaque sous-partie, la présence des termes, les liens réellement rendus, les explications citées et les renvois à un traitement antérieur.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-06 — exhaustive review of complex notions in introductions

requirements.statement: Lors de la modification d’une page Débat ou Argument existante, tout paramètre top-level autorisé attesté comme présent reste présent ; les profils de création ne peuvent pas le supprimer.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-07 — distinguish creation from modification and preserve existing parameters
requirements.note: Une suppression exige une décision explicite page/paramètre ou une exception spécialisée.

requirements.statement: Les avertissements et métadonnées historiques d’une page préexistante ne reçoivent jamais les valeurs par défaut réservées à une création IA et sont préservés exactement par défaut.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-07 — preserve warnings and existing metadata

requirements.statement: Le validateur confronte les paramètres présents des pages historiques à l’inventaire source et bloque toute disparition non explicitement autorisée.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-07 — no silent parameter deletion

requirements.title: Recherche des noms consacrés des arguments nouveaux
requirements.statement: Every new Argument page must have a documented literature search for a conventional argument name. The default outcome is none; nom-consacré/established-name may be rendered only when the literature attests the same reasoning under that label. Legacy nom/name is preservation-only for attested pre-existing pages.

English translation is performed in closed editorial review units: the Debate page is standalone; Argument review units contain 10 pages by default, shrink to 5–8 when documentary or terminological density is high, and may be aggregated into larger delivery bundles only after each internal unit is independently closed; an Argument page is never split.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-07 — English translation batches and documentary adaptation

requirements.statement: After all Argument batches, a global cross-batch review checks terminology, titles, bilingual vocabulary, conventional argument names, documentation, translated quotes and graph parity before English finalization.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-07 — English translation batches and documentary adaptation

requirements.statement: English Argument name is researched independently in English-language literature and is never mechanically translated or stylistically normalized from French; competing attested constructions are compared, the conventional English syntax is preserved, and the label must cover the exact logical scope of the page rather than only a subvariant, author-specific form or partial reasoning.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-07 — English translation batches and documentary adaptation

requirements.statement: A French reference is never converted into an English reference by translating its notice or title. It is projected to an English page only when a real English edition, translation, official version, original English publication or other verified English-language equivalent exists, using that version's own metadata.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-07 — English translation batches and documentary adaptation

requirements.statement: English documentation includes an independent search for new relevant English-language references and is not limited to English equivalents of the French selection.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-07 — English translation batches and documentary adaptation

requirements.statement: The reference-adaptation rule does not alter the special Citation-to-Quote contract: only quote text and linguistic date form are translated, all other documentary values remain exact, and AI-translated quote is appended once to warnings.
sources: owner decision 2026-08-07 — English translation batches and documentary adaptation

requirements.statement: Les règles éditoriales actives sont cumulatives et s’appliquent indépendamment de la valeur de normative_versions.consolidated_norm; ce numéro ne sert pas de feature flag éditorial.
requirements.enforcement: Schémas sans garde de version et tests statiques/d’invariance du validateur.
requirements.note: Introduit en 1.2.54.

requirements.statement: Les champs historiques *_policy_revision et *_revision sont des métadonnées de traçabilité et ne peuvent ni activer ni désactiver une norme éditoriale.
requirements.enforcement: Absence de comparaisons conditionnelles de ces métadonnées dans les contrôles éditoriaux.
requirements.note: Les valeurs existantes restent acceptées pour la reproductibilité.

requirements.statement: Les versions globales peuvent piloter la lecture ou la migration d’un ancien format, tandis que la version de format d’un artefact est portée par son propre schema, schema_version ou identifiant version stable.
